messages:
sam: FYI customer reported CI started failing after we published a tagged v2 release and they have a replace in go.mod. Error looks like a proxy/auth issue, but could be module path mismatch. Repro steps below.

sam: logs:
```
go: github.com/acme/lib@v2.1.0: reading from https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/acme/lib/@v/v2.1.0.zip: 401 Unauthorized
go: error loading module requirements
```

sam: go.mod snippet they shared:
```
module github.com/example/app

require (
  github.com/acme/lib v2.1.0
)

replace github.com/acme/lib => github.com/acme/lib v2.1.0
```

sam: CI env: GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct, GOPRIVATE=github.com/acme, no custom .netrc in job. They claim it worked pre-release and broke after tag publish.

kevin: can you paste the full `go env` from the failing runner and `go mod why`? also does the module's go.mod have `/v2` suffix in the module path?

sam: pasted `go env` (relevant):
```
GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct
GOPRIVATE=github.com/acme
GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org
```

sam: and the library's go.mod: `module github.com/acme/lib` (no /v2) — but tag is v2.1.0. customer says upstream module did not add /v2 path.

liz: that is the classic semver v2+ module path mismatch. If the module is semver v2 but module path didn't include `/v2`, clients can get weird checksum/proxy errors. But 401 from proxy implies proxy rejected access. Could be a combination: proxy tried to fetch and hit private repo and failed auth.

jon: customer uses replace to point at the tagged release rather than a local path; that can confuse the proxy resolution. In CI `replace` to a local path works locally but fails in CI when the path is absent.

sam: minimal repro I pushed (private): https://git.internal/acme/repro-go-mod-2481234567 (internal) — contains two modules: lib@v2 tag with module path missing /v2 and a consumer that requires v2.1.0 with replace pointing at the tag URL.

kevin: thanks. quick triage checklist: 1) confirm CI runner has credentials for the proxy/private git host, 2) ensure GOPRIVATE/GONOSUMDB set correctly in CI, 3) check module path vs tag (module must be `github.com/acme/lib/v2` for tags v2+), 4) avoid replace to remote tag in CI — use local replace or update to correct module path/tag.

sam: did 1 & 2 with customer — CI had no git auth, they're relying on anonymous access which used to work because proxy cached older zip, but new tag caused proxy to fetch upstream and hit 401. Customer's corporate firewall blocks access to git from our runners without token.

liz: immediate mitigation for customer: either add auth token to CI for git access or republish the module with corrected module path (module github.com/acme/lib/v2). Longer term we should document this edge case in support KB.

jon: customer asked for a workaround they can do right now. Suggestion: locally vendor the dependency or use `GOPRIVATE` + `GONOSUMDB='github.com/acme'` and configure netrc/token in CI so proxy will fetch successfully.

sam: tried vendor approach and it works (go env GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor), but they can't commit vendor by policy. They asked us to escalate because they think a Redwood change caused this.

kevin: not a platform bug — external tag + missing /v2 is upstream, and CI auth is missing. Still, we should verify we didn't change any proxy settings. @infra-bot can you confirm there were no config changes to our proxy or published docs around GOPRIVATE in the last 2 weeks?

infra-bot: Deploy audit: no changes to GOPROXY/GONOSUMDB configs in the last 14 days. Ticket created INFRA-4523 to audit proxy access logs for that fetch (linked in ticket).

sam: next steps for support: 1) provide the customer with a minimal writeup (module path v2 rule + CI auth). 2) share repro and recommended mitigations. 3) offer help adding token to their CI (we can run a quick test job).

liz: I'll draft the KB note and include a short checklist: check module path, avoid remote replace in CI, confirm CI git/proxy creds, vendor as last resort.

kevin: +1. Assign to eng-infra for the proxy log check and keep thread updated. Customer is happy with vendor workaround for now. :thumbsup:
